title: Engagement ignition: GrowthWave 30-day POC charter
content:
Context and high-level goal:
GrowthWave is a mid-market personalization SaaS exploring Redwood to power a customer-facing recommendations assistant (long-tail product suggestions + short explanation). They want to validate cost/latency across representative traffic and confirm quality on 12 canonical prompts.

This doc captures the 30-day POC charter, the workshop plan for Day 0, acceptance criteria, minimal integration checklist, roles, and immediate risks. Use this as the single source-of-truth for the Solutions + GrowthWave workstream.

TL;DR milestones (30 days)
- Day 0: Alignment workshop and infra handshake (this doc + API keys + sample dataset)
- Day 0–7: Integration + small-scale hosted runs (100k tokens total) to measure baseline latency/cost
- Day 8–18: Load experiments on Dedicated config + caching/batching trials (simulate 50 rps bursts)
- Day 19–26: Quality validation against 12 canonical prompts and 150 in-the-wild examples, iterate prompts
- Day 27–30: Acceptance test run, handoff brief, next-step proposal (Dedicated commit sizing or Hosted go-live)

Primary success hypothesis
"If we can achieve median tail latency <= 150 ms for 95% of production-like requests and maintain API cost below $0.0009/token with model-variant fallbacks while keeping human-judged quality >= 85% on the canonical prompts, GrowthWave will commit to a limited production pilot."

Quantitative acceptance criteria (must meet ALL):
- Latency: P95 end-to-end (client -> Redwood -> model -> client) <= 150 ms for canonical prompt set under steady-state test profile (10 rps).
- Throughput resilience: sustain 50 rps 30s bursts with automatic fallback to lower-cost variant with no more than 10% request failures.
- Cost: observed token cost (including dedup and batching effects) <= $0.0009/token on average over a 24-hour representative window.
- Quality: human evaluation pass-rate >= 85% (binary helpful/not-helpful) across the 12 canonical prompts plus a 150-sample in-the-wild set.
- Security/compliance: customer data is encrypted at rest and in transit; sample logs redaction applied per their policy (no PII in test logs).

Qualitative acceptance (informal but tracked):
- Product team satisfied with the coherency and rationale in model outputs (short explainers).
- SRE/ops confirm rollout policy and observability hooks are sufficient for pilot.

MVP scope for POC (explicitly constrained)
- Feature: recommendation text + 1-sentence explanation. No multi-turn conversation, no tools.
- Data: anonymized product catalog (top 3 categories), purchase signals (aggregated), and 1 week of clickstream sample (anonymized).
- Integrations: Redwood Hosted API for quick ramp; optional Dedicated trial if latency targets not met with Hosted.
- Instrumentation: token-level cost logs, route-level latency traces, sampling of 10% of responses stored for eval (PII redacted).

Minimal integration checklist (engineer-to-engineer)
- [ ] API access: GrowthWave service account + Redwood test token created (Rafael to confirm).
- [ ] Sample dataset: product catalog CSV (<= 5k rows) and 150 example user queries delivered to solutions-engineering bucket (Priya).
- [ ] Network: IP allowlist if needed; VPC peering discussion only if Dedicated is chosen.
- [ ] Logging: confirm sampling policy and redaction flow (Samir).
- [ ] Monitoring: provide SLI list to Redwood (latency, error-rate, cost-per-token) and setup dashboard link.
- [ ] Eval harness: shared spreadsheet with canonical prompts + scoring rubric.

Day 0 Workshop agenda (90 minutes)
- 0–10: Introductions, shared objectives (Maya)
- 10–25: GrowthWave product context and target UX (customer product PM)
- 25–40: Redwood integration model options & tradeoffs (Hosted vs Dedicated) (Maya + Evelyn)
- 40–60: Walk through canonical prompts and quality rubric (interactive scoring)
- 60–75: Ops handshake — credentials, logging, SLO targets (Samir)
- 75–90: Risks, open questions, immediate action items & owners (all)

Roles & RACI (short)
- Customer (GrowthWave PM): owns product acceptance, provides datasets and canonical prompts (R: GrowthWave PM)
- Solutions Engineer (Maya): technical direction, integration help, run correlation experiments (A: Maya)
- Integration Engineer (Rafael): implement the API calls, dataset ingestion, CI scripts (R: Rafael)
- SRE/Observability (Samir): configure dashboards, validate SLO measurement (R: Samir)
- Product Eng / On-call (GrowthWave): support customer-side changes and deploy feature flags (C: GrowthWave eng)

Acceptance test matrix (how we'll verify)
- Test 1: Steady-state latency run (10 rps, canonical prompts) -> collect P95, P99. Pass if P95 <= 150 ms.
- Test 2: Burst resiliency (simulate 50 rps bursts for 30s every 5 min for 1 hour) -> pass if < 10% errors and fallback invoked gracefully.
- Test 3: Cost window (24h sampling) -> measured token unit-cost <= threshold.
- Test 4: Quality eval -> blinded human raters score helpful/not helpful on 162 prompts (12 canonical + 150 in-the-wild). Pass threshold >= 85%.

Open technical risks and mitigations
- Risk: Catalog contains sparse descriptions that lead to low-quality recommendations. Mitigation: temporarily augment product rows with templated descriptors (script) and re-run.
- Risk: Batching strategies increase tail latency on short prompts. Mitigation: tune batching thresholds; use per-route special-case for short prompts.
- Risk: Observability gaps for token-level cost attribution. Mitigation: enable debug token logs during test window (redacted) and run comparator jobs.

Operational notes / heuristics gathered from past POCs
- Start with Hosted to validate quality quickly; move to Dedicated only if sustained latency/cost wins are expected.
- Use a two-tier model routing policy: default to best-quality variant, fallback to low-cost variant on capacity signals.
- Keep canonical prompt set small but diverse; add synthetic hard-cases early.

Immediate next steps (post-workshop) — owners & deadlines
- Rafael: create test-service-account + deliver keys to SEs (by Day 1 end).
- Priya: drop product catalog + 150 queries into the shared bucket (by Day 2).
- Samir: provision dashboard skeleton & SLO probes (by Day 3).
- Maya: schedule paired integration session + run initial 10k token smoke tests (by Day 4).

Notes to self / informal points (copy to workshop minutes)
- Keep communications in slack channel: #cust-growthwave-onboarding — pin this doc.
- Track all performance runs with a simple spreadsheet: date, config, model, tokens, cost, P95, P99.
- If cost is > target but quality good, capture sample outputs and run a manual review to explore quantization or prompts to reduce tokens.

Decision log (placeholder)
- 2025-11-02: Agreed to start on Hosted with option to trial Dedicated after Day 10 experiments. (decision: provisional)

Appendix: quick scoring rubric for human eval
- 0 = not helpful / incorrect recommendation
- 1 = partially helpful (wrong rank or missing context)
- 2 = helpful and actionable (meets product expectation)

End of charter.
